text: Communication is generally direct with the Seychellois.

Personal space is does not tend to be highly valued. Less than an arm's length is usually the norm. People generally have very few boundaries, which can be disconcerting to many Westerners. Light touching during conversations is very common with whoever one is interacting with.
Direct eye contact is desirable and expected in most situations.

Time tends to be a truly fluid concept in the Seychelles. Punctuality is not valued much at all, though some effort is made in business situations. People are very generous and giving with their time.

Seychelles is a matriarchal society. The women tend to be the ones who run businesses and are also very present in the government. They may dress as they please and are generally very free. is a predominantly Catholic country and old-fashioned attitudes towards the sexual behavior of women prevail. (Note that this is somewhat hypocritical, as most women are not overly modest.)

The thumbs up sign is a very common gesture and is used to denote general satisfaction, often upon greeting. Pointing is done with one finger. The length of an object is shown by marking the place on the arm with the forefinger, from tip of the hand.

There is a dress code in the evenings. Men have to wear long trousers and women are encouraged to dress up (no shorts and/or beach wear). Women should not be too friendly and open with the men, as this is often misconstrued for sexual interest.

The legal drinking and smoking age is 18. They are not at all heavily enforced and consumption of alcohol is widespread amongst the youth. Penalties for possession of illegal drugs are heavy and enforced. Nonetheless, there is heavy use of marijuana and, more recently, heroin. Aside from law enforcement for drug use, not many laws are enforced. Drunk driving, for instance, is very common and usually overlooked. The police themselves are often guilty of this crime.
For Men - Fairly casual, long trousers and a shirt, no tie needed in most situations. For Women - Knee length skirts and a blouse.

Usually, even in a business setting, first names are used nowadays. Amongst the older generation, surnames with a Mr. or Mrs. may be used. If people give out business cards at all, which is rare, it is usually given with one hand.
Meetings tend to be very casual in the Seychelles. Some measure of punctuality is expected, but meetings usually proceed on an ad hoc basis.
Bargaining is not common. Decisions are made fairly quickly and negotiations are very up front.
Gifts are not common in business settings.
The local schools begin in January and have their long vacation in December. The international school follows the British school calendar.
Drinking and smoking are fully accepted. People are often excessively drunk in public, even to the point of falling down. When it comes to dating, both sexes tend to be very forward.

민족, 종교, 언어 - 인구 90%가 크리올 혈통으로 프랑스, 영국, 아프리카, 중국, 중동을 포함한 다양한 출신의 초기 정착민과 상인의 후손 2. 언론 인 도-세이셸인(Indo-Seychellois)은 세이셸에서 두 번째로 큰 민족으로 4. 북한과의 관계 - 1770년 15명의 프랑스 식민지 개척자들에 의해 아프리카인과 함께 노예로 끌려온 남인도인 - 추후 식민지 농장과 도로 건설 작업이 시작되면서 노예가 아닌 계약 노동자로 입국 - 대부분 마헤섬에 거주하며 농업, 제조 기업가, 도매업 및 무역업에 종사 - 대다수가 크리올어, 영어, 프랑스어 구사 시 노-세이셸(Sino-Seychellois) 중국인은 약 1,000명 - 1886년에 최초의 중국 이민자들이 세이셸 도착 - 대다수는 크리올어 및 영어와 프랑스어를 구사하며 대부분 기독교인 - 상점 관리, 운송 및 어업 분야 종사 SeychelleS 92 Republic of Ghana 세이셸 개황 93 Ⅶ 사회 문화 나.

신문 - 대학 진학 준비 과정 혹은 전문 직업훈련 목적 인쇄본과 온라인 형식 방식으로 정치, 경제, 스포츠, 문화 등 주제를 - 교육, 예술 및 디자인, 건설, 엔지니어링, 농업 교육 등 11개 과정 제공 다양하게 제공 - 중요한 동문: 장 폴 아담(Jean-Paul Adam) 전 외무부 장관(2010~2016년 재임) 일 간지 3.
